gem_cut.immersive_jewelry.round.descript: Balanced and forgiving: six facets, a fair share of the stone kept.
gem_cut.immersive_jewelry.brilliant.desc: Ten facets that make the stone blaze: the strongest expression of its trait, the most waste and the most risk.
gem_cut.immersive_jewelry.emerald.descri: Long steps and narrow corners: steady, keeps much of the stone, and its effects last longer.
gem_cut.immersive_jewelry.cabochon.descr: A smooth dome in four wide passes: very forgiving and kind to opaque stones, but gentle in effect.
finish.immersive_jewelry.polished.descri: Bright and brilliant: the stone speaks louder, though the frame shows wear sooner. Takes Polishing Compound.
finish.immersive_jewelry.burnished.descr: Rubbed hard and muted: a sturdier frame and steadier effects, a little less brilliance. No material needed.
finish.immersive_jewelry.antique.descrip: Darkened recesses and old-world charm: takes enchantment far better and favours magic. Takes gunpowder for the patina.

jei.immersive_jewelry.remove_text: Open each prong gently with the pliers and lift the stone out with the tweezers: the stones come back, the frame keeps a little wear.
jei.immersive_jewelry.repair_text: True the frame with the burnisher. One nugget of its metal restores Integrity, less after every rework.
jei.immersive_jewelry.recut_text: A chipped or poorly cut stone can be cut again, smaller.
jei.immersive_jewelry.info.blanks_smithi: Forged with Immersive Smithing: melt a little metal in the Smith's Forge, shape it on the Smith's Anvil (a short, precise job) and quench it. The metal and the quality of the smithing carry into the jewelry.
jei.immersive_jewelry.info.blanks_fallba: Crafted from nuggets of any metal at a crafting table. A crafted blank has only middling metalwork; with Immersive Smithing installed, blanks are forged instead.
jei.immersive_jewelry.info.wheel: Use the wheel holding a gemstone (a diamond, an emerald, amethyst, lapis, quartz, a modded gem or a rough stone) to mount it, then step up to it with an empty hand: plan a cut at the specimen rack and grind each face on the turning lap with the handle. A lap upgrades the wheel.
jei.immersive_jewelry.info.bench: Use the bench holding a blank, cut stones, Jeweler's Pliers or a finish material to lay them out, then sit down at it with an empty hand: choose a design in the folio, seat the stones with the tweezers, close the setting and finish the piece by hand. Finished pieces are reworked here too. The Jeweler's workstation.
jei.immersive_jewelry.info.pliers: Dock them at a Jeweler's Bench to close, retighten and open prongs. Better pliers give a wider secure band. Bezels are closed with the bench's own pusher.
jei.immersive_jewelry.info.lap: Fit it to a Lapidary Wheel by using the wheel with it: faster grinding, wider depth windows, steadier sweeps and cooler stones. Wears a little with every cut.
jei.immersive_jewelry.info.sketch: Teaches an advanced design. Bought from Jewelers or found in treasure.
jei.immersive_jewelry.info.gem_dust: All that is left of a stone that shattered. Makes Polishing Compound.
jei.immersive_jewelry.info.jewelry: Each piece is unique: its metal, stones, cut, finish and your workmanship decide what it does. Wear it in a jewelry slot.

handbook.immersive_jewelry.welcome.title: The Jeweler's Craft
handbook.immersive_jewelry.welcome.0: Jewelry is made here, not crafted. A piece is its stones, its metal and the care you put into it.
handbook.immersive_jewelry.welcome.1: Cut a stone on the Lapidary Wheel. Forge a blank. Set the stone by hand at the Jeweler's Bench and finish it. Then wear it: what it does comes from what it is made of, and how well.
handbook.immersive_jewelry.welcome.2: Step up to a station with an empty hand to work at it. Leave whenever you like: the work waits on the stone or on the bench.
handbook.immersive_jewelry.stones.title: Gemstones
handbook.immersive_jewelry.stones.0: Diamonds, emeralds, amethyst, lapis and quartz are rough stones as they are; so are the gems of other mods.
handbook.immersive_jewelry.stones.1: Rubies, sapphires, topaz and onyx also turn up rough in treasure and at the Jeweler.
handbook.immersive_jewelry.stones.2: When a stone first reaches the wheel it is appraised: its size, its clarity (few inclusions is better) and its luster. That character never changes.
handbook.immersive_jewelry.wheel.title: The Lapidary Wheel
handbook.immersive_jewelry.wheel.0: Use the wheel holding a stone to mount it, or holding a lap to fit the lap. Use it with an empty hand to step up to it; sneak-use with an empty hand takes the stone back.
handbook.immersive_jewelry.wheel.1: The specimen rack beside the lap shows the cuts this stone allows: choose one to plan it. Until the first grind you can change your mind freely.
handbook.immersive_jewelry.wheel.2: A lap improves the wheel: an Emery Lap grinds faster and steadier, a Diamond Lap faster still, with wider depth windows and cooler stones. Laps wear with every cut.
handbook.immersive_jewelry.cutting.title: Cutting
handbook.immersive_jewelry.cutting.0: Take the handle and lower the stone onto the turning lap: how far you press is the force. Sweep it smoothly across. Too fast and it rocks, held still it grinds a flat spot, too hard and it scratches.
handbook.immersive_jewelry.cutting.1: A brass line on the stone marks the face's depth, and the grinding sounds brighter as you near it. Lift, turn the collar to the next face and lower again; opposite faces in turn keep the stone true.
handbook.immersive_jewelry.cutting.2: The stone warms as it works: lift it, or dip it in the cooling cup. Too hot and it chips. The loupe shows every face up close. When all are cut, pull the release lever.
handbook.immersive_jewelry.cutting.3: With the keyboard, hold the tool key to grind: the stone sweeps by itself.
handbook.immersive_jewelry.cuts.title: Choosing a Cut
handbook.immersive_jewelry.cuts.0: Cabochon: four broad zones, domed by keeping the stone moving. Very forgiving, kind to opaque stones, gentle in effect.$(br)Round: six facets, balanced.
handbook.immersive_jewelry.cuts.1: Emerald: long steps first, then the corners; keeps more stone and its effects last longer.$(br)Brilliant: ten facets, the strongest effect, the most waste and the most risk.
handbook.immersive_jewelry.cuts.2: Hard stones grind slowly; brittle and included ones chip sooner.
handbook.immersive_jewelry.blanks.title: Blanks and Frames
handbook.immersive_jewelry.blanks.0: The metal part of a piece is forged.
handbook.immersive_jewelry.blanks.1: With Immersive Smithing, a ring blank, amulet frame, bracelet blank or circlet frame is a small job at the Smith's Forge and Anvil, in any metal it knows. Your smithing quality is kept.
handbook.immersive_jewelry.blanks.2: Without it, blanks are crafted from nuggets at a crafting table, with middling metalwork.
handbook.immersive_jewelry.bench.title: The Jeweler's Bench
handbook.immersive_jewelry.bench.0: Use the bench holding a blank or a finished piece (it goes in the clamp), cut stones (the tray), Jeweler's Pliers (the dock) or a finish material (the jars).
handbook.immersive_jewelry.bench.1: Sneak-use with an empty hand takes things back. Then sit down at it with an empty hand.
handbook.immersive_jewelry.bench.2: The folio holds the designs for the piece in the clamp, the stones each needs and the finishes it allows. Pick up the tweezers, take a stone from the tray and let it go into its cup: how straight it lands is its seat.
handbook.immersive_jewelry.bench.3: Until the first prong closes, everything can still come off the bench. Leave at any time: the work stays on the bench, or pack it as an unfinished piece and carry it away.
handbook.immersive_jewelry.bench.4: The bench is also the Jeweler villager's workstation.
handbook.immersive_jewelry.setting.title: Setting a Stone
handbook.immersive_jewelry.setting.0: With the pliers, grip a prong and squeeze until it meets the stone, then let go to check. Short of the stone it stays loose;
handbook.immersive_jewelry.setting.1: pushed past, it leans in and may chip a brittle stone. Close opposite prongs in turn and the stone sits level.
handbook.immersive_jewelry.setting.2: A bezel is closed with the bench's pusher: press the rim in and sweep round it evenly.
handbook.immersive_jewelry.setting.3: The loupe shows each point and how the stone sits. When every stone is held, confirm and go on to the finish.
handbook.immersive_jewelry.finishes.0: Polished: brighter and stronger stones, a frame that wears sooner. Rubbed in with cloth and Polishing Compound.$(br)Burnished: a tougher frame and steadier effects. Worked with the burnisher.
handbook.immersive_jewelry.finishes.1: Antique: darker recesses, far better enchanting, a touch more magic. Brushed on with gunpowder, then the high points wiped bright.
handbook.immersive_jewelry.finishes.2: Work the tool over the whole piece evenly. A finished piece can be refinished at the bench.
handbook.immersive_jewelry.wearing.title: Wearing Jewelry
handbook.immersive_jewelry.wearing.0: Rings, amulets, bracelets and circlets are worn in jewelry slots: two rings, one of each other form. With Curios they use its slots; otherwise open the jewelry slots from the ring button in your inventory or with J.
handbook.immersive_jewelry.wearing.1: Your workmanship combines metalwork, the cut and the setting.
handbook.immersive_jewelry.effects.title: What Jewelry Does
handbook.immersive_jewelry.effects.0: Each gem has a theme and each form expresses it differently. A ruby ring builds heat with every hit; a ruby amulet saves you when you are nearly beaten; a ruby bracelet rewards a charge.
handbook.immersive_jewelry.effects.1: The metal biases it (gold favours magic, silver protection, copper answers quickly), the cut sets its strength and steadiness, and the finish tunes it. Read a piece's tooltip for its numbers.
handbook.immersive_jewelry.care.title: Care and Repair
handbook.immersive_jewelry.care.0: Jewelry does not wear in ordinary fighting, only under heavy blows. A worn frame is repaired from the rework page of the bench's folio: true it with the burnisher. One nugget of its metal restores it, a little less fully after every rework.
handbook.immersive_jewelry.care.1: From the same page a piece is retightened, or taken apart: open each prong gently with the pliers and lift the stone out with the tweezers. A chipped stone is recut at the wheel, smaller but whole.
handbook.immersive_jewelry.designs.title: Designs
handbook.immersive_jewelry.designs.0: Solitaire and bezel rings, pendant and locket amulets, cuffs and simple circlets are known to every jeweler.
handbook.immersive_jewelry.designs.1: Richer designs with three stones - the trilogy ring, halo amulet, link bracelet and diadem - are learned from Design Sketches, found in treasure or bought from Jewelers.
handbook.immersive_jewelry.jeweler.title: The Jeweler
handbook.immersive_jewelry.jeweler.0: A villager who claims a Jeweler's Bench becomes a Jeweler.
handbook.immersive_jewelry.jeweler.1: Jewelers trade rough and cut stones, pliers, laps, sketches and, at the highest level, a piece of village work: good, but never a masterwork. That is yours to make.

workstation.immersive_jewelry.drawer.key: [%s] to the bench · [%s] to the inventory · [%s] open/shut · arrows: choose
book.immersive_jewelry.title: Jeweler's Handbook
book.immersive_jewelry.subtitle: The jeweler's craft, step by step
book.immersive_jewelry.landing: A stone, a frame and the care you give them. This handbook follows a piece from the rough stone to the hand that wears it. Press $(k:key.immersive_jewelry.handbook) at a station for the page about the step in front of you.
book.immersive_jewelry.category.start.de: The route from stone to wearable, the two stations, the tools, the controls, and how to leave and come back to work.
book.immersive_jewelry.category.stones.d: Where stones come from, what appraisal fixes for good, and every gem this world knows.
book.immersive_jewelry.category.wheel.de: Mounting, planning and grinding a cut, the four cuts, and recutting a damaged stone.
book.immersive_jewelry.category.metal.de: The four forms, their blanks, how blanks are made here, and the metals.
The design folio, sketches and every design this world knows.
Seating stones, closing prongs and bezels, several stones in one piece, and what can go wrong.
book.immersive_jewelry.category.finishin: Polished, burnished and antique finishes, their costs, and refinishing a piece.
Slots, what a piece does and why, and when a piece does nothing.
book.immersive_jewelry.category.care.des: Wear, repair, retightening, taking a piece apart, recutting and safe keeping.
book.immersive_jewelry.category.workshop: Jewelers, working beside other players, and other mods.
When something is refused or missing, and what packs and mods can change.
book.immersive_jewelry.start.welcome.0: Every station key, every option and every rule of this world is in this book, and the cards marked $(o)Live$() read them from the server you are on.
book.immersive_jewelry.start.welcome.wat: A whole piece, from a rough diamond to a worn ring.
book.immersive_jewelry.start.first_piece: A first ring: a diamond, a round cut and a solitaire setting. Mount the diamond on a $(l:immersive_jewelry:wheel/wheel)Lapidary Wheel$(/l) with a lap fitted; it is appraised once and for all.
Plan the round cut at the specimen rack, then grind each face to its depth line, lifting and cooling as the stone warms. Pull the release lever: you hold a cut diamond.

Make a ring blank (see $(l:immersive_jewelry:metal/blanks)Blanks$(/l)) and put it in the clamp of a $(l:immersive_jewelry:setting/bench)Jeweler's Bench$(/l) with the diamond in the tray and pliers in the dock. Pick the Solitaire Ring in the folio.
Seat the stone with the tweezers, close the four prongs with the pliers, confirm, and polish with cloth and compound. Take the ring and wear it in a ring slot.
Watch the same route, start to finish.
book.immersive_jewelry.start.stations.0: The Lapidary Wheel cuts stones; the Jeweler's Bench sets them, finishes pieces and reworks them. Better tools are real items: their tiers and wear are on the next page.
book.immersive_jewelry.start.stations.wa: Laps and pliers, and the fixtures that are not items.
book.immersive_jewelry.start.controls.0: Use a station with an empty hand to step up to it. The mouse takes handles and tools; every action also has a key. Press $(k:key.immersive_jewelry.handbook) at a station for help: tap for the page, hold for a demonstration.
book.immersive_jewelry.start.controls.1: Comfort options (client config, workstation): no zoom, instant camera moves, hold or toggle the tool key, sticky drag, larger targets, numbers beside the work, hints, visual cues for sounds, and calmer motion.
book.immersive_jewelry.start.controls.2: Presentation options: bodyAnimation (full, reduced, off) for jewelers' poses, reducedTutorialMotion for the demonstrations, and the worn-jewelry switches. None of them changes what you make.
book.immersive_jewelry.start.leaving.0: Leave a station whenever you like: Escape, walking off, a hit or a teleport ends your turn at once. Tools lift; nothing finishes, refunds or disappears.
book.immersive_jewelry.start.leaving.1: A part-cut stone carries its work in its own data: take it to any wheel and go on. A bench keeps its work; pack it as an $(o)Unfinished$() piece to carry it, frame, stones and all.
book.immersive_jewelry.start.leaving.2: Opening this book or a demonstration from a station leaves the station first. The world does not pause; when you come back, use the station again to continue.
book.immersive_jewelry.start.leaving.wat: Take a part-cut stone away and finish it elsewhere.
book.immersive_jewelry.stones.sources.0: Gems found through tags (forge:gems/...) count as rough stones automatically, with a neutral trait. Ruby, sapphire, topaz and onyx also come rough from treasure and Jewelers when no mod adds them.
book.immersive_jewelry.stones.sources.wa: A source item becomes one appraised stone.
Appraisal happens once, when a stone first reaches a wheel. It fixes three things for good: size, natural quality (luster) and inclusions (clarity).
Taking the stone off, planning another cut, reading, relogging or changing the lap never rolls it again.
Size is how much stone there is; cutting removes some. Natural quality is what the stone can become. Cut quality is what you made of it. A fine cut cannot exceed what the stone allows.
Inclusions and brittleness make a stone chip sooner. Damage goes scratched, chipped, fractured; only a recut at the wheel clears it. Opaque stones (lapis, onyx) suit the cabochon.
book.immersive_jewelry.stones.gems.0: The cards that follow are this world's gems, read live: their trait, hardness, the cuts they take (★ favoured) and their source items. The last card lists gems found automatically.
book.immersive_jewelry.wheel.wheel.watch: Index, grind, lift and inspect a round cut.
book.immersive_jewelry.wheel.cutting.wat: The round cut: six even faces.
The brilliant: ten faces, more care near the depth.
The emerald cut: long steps first, then the corners.
The cabochon: a dome, the stone always moving.
book.immersive_jewelry.wheel.recutting.0: Too much force scratches, a fast sweep rocks the stone, a still stone flattens, and heat chips. Each mistake stays on the stone and lowers the cut's quality.
book.immersive_jewelry.wheel.recutting.1: A chipped or fractured stone, cut or set, can be recut: mount it and plan a cut again. A recut starts from the stone as it is now and keeps only the cut's share of that size.
book.immersive_jewelry.wheel.recutting.2: A stone ground away entirely becomes Gem Grit, which makes Polishing Compound. Recutting is for real damage, not to chase a better roll: the appraisal never changes.
book.immersive_jewelry.wheel.recutting.w: An overheated stone, and what a recut costs.
book.immersive_jewelry.metal.blanks.watc: The four blanks, and where each route applies.
book.immersive_jewelry.metal.forms.0: Four forms: the ring (ring blank), amulet (amulet frame), bracelet (bracelet blank) and circlet (circlet frame). A blank keeps its metal, its smithing quality and its maker's history.
book.immersive_jewelry.metal.forms.1: The form decides how a gem's trait shows: a ring answers each blow, an amulet guards, a bracelet rewards movement, a circlet sharpens the mind. See $(l:immersive_jewelry:wearing/effects)Effects$(/l).
book.immersive_jewelry.metal.forms.2: Finished pieces with stones are never melted down by Immersive Smithing's recycling, and an unfinished piece cannot be recycled either: take it apart at the bench first.
book.immersive_jewelry.metal.metals.0: Every metal changes a piece a little: some strengthen effects, some the frame, some enchanting. The metals with a jewelry definition here are listed next.
book.immersive_jewelry.metal.metals.1: Any other metal works too, with a neutral profile and the colour and name it was forged with. Repairs use a nugget (or ingot) of the piece's own metal.
book.immersive_jewelry.designs.folio.0: The folio lies on the bench. It lists the designs for the frame in the clamp, the stones each needs and the finishes it allows. Starred designs can be shown alone.
book.immersive_jewelry.designs.folio.1: A locked design shows what it needs and why it is locked. The folio can bring matching cut stones from your inventory to the tray: exactly those stones, nothing else.
book.immersive_jewelry.designs.folio.2: Choosing a design costs nothing. Everything can still come off the bench until the first prong closes or the first effective finishing stroke.
book.immersive_jewelry.designs.folio.wat: A known and a locked design, and learning a sketch.
Use a Design Sketch to learn its design; the sketch is used up. Reading this book or watching a demonstration teaches nothing. The server may not require sketches at all:
book.immersive_jewelry.designs.atlas.0: The ten designs that come with the mod, read from this server's recipes, then designs added by packs. Each card shows the setting, the stone count, what it allows and whether you know it.
book.immersive_jewelry.designs.preparati: The folio has a search field: click it (or press / or Ctrl+F) and type a name, gem, cut or finish. While it has the keyboard every key is text; Escape leaves the field first, and only a second Escape closes the folio. Filters show known sketches, designs for the clamped frame, and designs whose stones you have.

The staging drawer in front of the vise holds four loose stacks: stones, frames, pliers or supplies you want at hand. Open it with its brass pull or the drawer key; put stacks down by hand and they stay where you leave them. Shut, it hides them and takes nothing. Nothing is ever used from the drawer by itself.

The three glass jars are the supplies: polishing compound, gunpowder, nuggets or repair metal. Click, split, shift-click and the mouse wheel work on them as on any container slot, and their counts face you. A finish takes its material from the jars at its first stroke; until then you can take it back.

In the folio, Prepare stones shows the stones that fit the design: gem, cut, quality, damage and where they are. Keep the best cuts, or choose a gem and click the stones you prefer. The bench then moves exactly the stones still needed into the tray and tells you what moved and what is missing.
The drawer, the jars and preparing a design's stones.
book.immersive_jewelry.setting.prongs.wa: Seat a stone and close opposite prongs in turn.
book.immersive_jewelry.setting.bezels.0: A bezel is a continuous rim, not a set of prongs. Take the bench's pusher, press the rim in and sweep it round the stone in even passes. No pliers are needed.
book.immersive_jewelry.setting.bezels.1: Work the whole rim: a rim closed on one side only holds the stone crooked. The loupe shows each section; the stone is held when every section meets it.
book.immersive_jewelry.setting.bezels.wa: Close a bezel evenly, all the way round.
book.immersive_jewelry.setting.multi_sto: Trilogy, halo, link and diadem designs take three stones of the same gem. Each stays its own stone, with its own size, cut, quality and history.
Seat each in its own cup and close each socket's prongs. The piece's quality follows all of them, so a weak third stone shows.
Three different appraised stones in one piece.
book.immersive_jewelry.setting.defects.0: Loose: a prong short of the stone. Bent: a prong pushed past it. Crooked: a stone seated off-centre or turned. Chipped: a brittle stone pinched too hard.
book.immersive_jewelry.setting.defects.1: Fine Pliers hold a closer tolerance than Jeweler's Pliers. Use the loupe before you confirm: what you leave now is kept on the piece.
book.immersive_jewelry.setting.defects.2: Loose and bent prongs and crooked stones can be corrected later by retightening. Polishing hides none of them.
book.immersive_jewelry.finishing.finishe: Polished: compound charged once, then even coverage.
Antique: patina dabbed on, high points wiped bright.
book.immersive_jewelry.finishing.refinis: A finished piece in the clamp opens the folio's rework page. Choose another finish the design allows and work it in like a new one; its material is used once.
Refinishing changes only the finish. It does not repair the frame, fix prongs or mend a chipped stone, and it counts as a rework of the frame.
A new finish on an old piece, and resuming packed work.
book.immersive_jewelry.wearing.slots.wat: Slots, limits, and how one gem shows on each form.
book.immersive_jewelry.wearing.effects.w: How workmanship, finish and defects show on the result.
book.immersive_jewelry.wearing.gates.0: A broken piece (no integrity left) does nothing until it is repaired; it is never destroyed. A piece without a stone, or with a stone of no known trait, does nothing either.
book.immersive_jewelry.wearing.gates.1: Beyond the server's slot limit, extra pieces of a form do nothing. Other mods may refuse a piece (a class or level rule); it then stays inert and says so.
book.immersive_jewelry.wearing.gates.2: Enchantments work as on other gear; the antique finish takes them best. Other mods can add effects to a piece (affixes, socketed gems); they keep their own power.
book.immersive_jewelry.care.rework.0: Put a finished piece in the bench's clamp to open the rework page. $(l)Repair$() trues the frame with the burnisher and one unit of its metal, up to a cap that falls with each rework.
book.immersive_jewelry.care.rework.1: $(l)Retighten$() reopens the setting with the pliers (a bezel with the pusher) so you can fix loose or bent points and crooked stones.
book.immersive_jewelry.care.rework.2: $(l)Take apart$() opens each prong gently and lifts each stone out with the tweezers. Every stone returns as it is; the frame goes back to a blank and loses some integrity.
book.immersive_jewelry.care.rework.3: A chipped or fractured stone goes to the wheel for a recut. Each repair, refinish or taking apart counts as a rework and lowers the repair cap a little.
book.immersive_jewelry.care.rework.watch: Retightening a setting versus repairing a frame.
Take the stones out and reuse them unchanged.
book.immersive_jewelry.care.storage.0: Broken jewelry keeps its stones, maker and history; repair it at a bench. Jewelry in chests, shulker boxes or ender chests does nothing and wears nothing.
book.immersive_jewelry.care.storage.1: An Unfinished piece holds its frame, its committed stones and its work. It cannot be worn or recycled; unpack it at any bench to continue.
book.immersive_jewelry.workshop.multipla: One player works a station at a time; others can stand by, watch the work and hear it. They cannot take a set stone, spend supplies or change the plan.
To hand over, leave the station; the next player steps up and continues the same work. Disconnecting or a hit ends a turn without losing anything. Design knowledge is each player's own.
Working, watching and handing over a station.
book.immersive_jewelry.workshop.integrat: With Curios, jewelry uses its ring, necklace, bracelet and head slots. With Immersive Smithing, blanks are forged at its forge and anvil and keep their smithing quality.
JEI shows cuts, designs and references; at a station its show-recipe and show-uses keys look up what is under the cursor. Jade shows a station's work, its stage and who is working.
Demonstrations use Ponder; it runs alone and with Create. Mods can add effects and rules to jewelry through the API (see $(l:immersive_jewelry:trouble/packs)For Pack Makers$(/l)).
book.immersive_jewelry.trouble.common.0: "This stone cannot take that cut": each gem allows certain cuts (diamond no cabochon, lapis only cabochon or round), and each design allows certain cuts and gems. The cards say which.
book.immersive_jewelry.trouble.common.1: A locked design needs its sketch learned. A design refused with another reason was refused by a rule of the server or of another mod; the message names it.
book.immersive_jewelry.trouble.common.2: No blank recipe? Blanks come from Immersive Smithing when it is installed and enabled; crafting fallbacks exist only when the server enables them. See the routes card under Blanks.
book.immersive_jewelry.trouble.common.3: A full inventory never loses a result: it waits on the station. An interrupted cut or setting is kept. A piece whose definition is missing keeps its data and shows as unavailable.
book.immersive_jewelry.trouble.packs.0: Datapacks add gems, cuts, finishes, forms, traits, metals and work profiles under data/<namespace>/immersive_jewelry/, and designs as recipes. Gem tags are found automatically.
book.immersive_jewelry.trouble.packs.1: Resource packs can restyle the stations, rigs, poses, this book and the demonstrations. They cannot make a disabled recipe work or widen a server's tolerances.
book.immersive_jewelry.trouble.packs.2: Mods can add effect types, effect contributions, equipment providers, craft, wear and assist rules, and listen to cut, craft, rework, equip and break events.
book.immersive_jewelry.watch.tooltip: Opens the demonstration; closing it returns to this page. Nothing in the world changes.
book.immersive_jewelry.card.unavailable: This card cannot show here (its data is missing).
book.immersive_jewelry.card.estimated: Estimated: a typical piece. Real pieces differ; their tooltip is exact.
book.immersive_jewelry.card.generic_none: None: every gem tag here has a definition.
book.immersive_jewelry.card.cost_none: none: the burnisher needs no reagent
book.immersive_jewelry.card.same_gem: All stones must be the same gem; each keeps its own data.
book.immersive_jewelry.card.route.none: No route is active: ask the server admin, or find blanks in trade.
book.immersive_jewelry.card.route.smithi: Forged blanks keep your smithing quality.
book.immersive_jewelry.card.metals_gener: Other metals use a neutral profile.
book.immersive_jewelry.card.inspect_hold: Hold a finished piece in your hand, then open this page.
book.immersive_jewelry.card.care.no_mate: needs its metal, which this world lacks
book.immersive_jewelry.card.care.defects: the setting has defects to fix
book.immersive_jewelry.card.care.secure: the setting is sound; it can still be reworked
book.immersive_jewelry.card.care.refinis: any other finish the design allows
book.immersive_jewelry.card.care.advisor: The bench checks again when the work starts.
book.immersive_jewelry.card.tools_wear: Pliers wear at a setting's first closure, a lap at a cut's first contact. Pausing never avoids or repeats it.
book.immersive_jewelry.card.severe_hit: A heavy hit is at least (of max health):
message.immersive_jewelry.tutorials_unav: Demonstrations need Ponder, which is not running.
message.immersive_jewelry.tutorial_missi: That demonstration could not be opened.
message.immersive_jewelry.handbook_unava: The Jeweler's Handbook could not be opened (Patchouli).
message.immersive_jewelry.help_return: Your work is as you left it. Use the station to continue.
message.immersive_jewelry.help_return_ch: The station or its work changed while you were reading. Look before you continue.
message.immersive_jewelry.drawer_cannot_: The staging drawer takes only the bench's own materials and tools.
message.immersive_jewelry.drawer_full: No room in the staging drawer.
message.immersive_jewelry.moved_part: Moved %s of %s; the rest stays in the drawer.
message.immersive_jewelry.prepare_ready: The bench already holds the %s stones this design needs.
message.immersive_jewelry.prepared_tray_: %s stone(s) moved; the tray is full, %s still missing.
message.immersive_jewelry.prepared_missi: %s stone(s) moved; %s still missing (not enough suitable stones of one gem).
immersive_jewelry.ponder.shared.example: Example: the numbers the mod ships with. Packs can change them; the handbook shows this server's.
immersive_jewelry.ponder.shared.first_pi: A rough diamond goes on the quill. It is appraised now, once and for good.
The specimen rack shows the cuts this stone allows. Pick the round cut.
Lower the stone onto the turning lap and sweep it. Lift to let it cool. (Shown faster than life.)
Every face is in its window: the release lever gives a cut diamond.
At the bench: a ring blank in the clamp, pliers in the dock, the stone in the tray, compound in a jar.
The Solitaire Ring from the folio. The stone is seated and its four prongs closed, opposite pairs in turn.
Polished with cloth and compound, the ring is finished.
Blanks come from Immersive Smithing, or from crafting where the server enables it.
immersive_jewelry.ponder.shared.watching: One jeweler works a station at a time.
Others can stand by and watch, but cannot take a stone, spend supplies or change the plan.
Leaving ends the turn. The work stays; the next jeweler continues the same piece.
Disconnecting or a hit ends a turn too: nothing is finished, refunded or lost.
immersive_jewelry.ponder.shared.appraisa: A source item (here a diamond) becomes one rough stone, appraised once: size, luster and clarity.
Taken off and mounted again, it is the same stone.
Nothing rerolls it: not a new plan, a relog, a lap change or reading the handbook.
Ruby, sapphire, topaz and onyx also come rough from treasure and Jewelers.
immersive_jewelry.ponder.shared.laps_and: An Emery Lap: faster and steadier than the bare wheel.
A Diamond Lap: faster still, wider depth windows, cooler stones.
A lap wears once per cut, at the first contact. Pausing does not repeat or avoid it.
Jeweler's Pliers in the dock close prongs.
Fine Pliers hold a closer tolerance.
Tweezers, pusher, burnisher, brush and cloth are the bench's own tools: no items needed.
immersive_jewelry.ponder.shared.round_cu: The round cut: six even radial faces.
Press lightly and sweep smoothly. A brass line marks each face's depth.
Lift, turn the collar to the next face, lower again. Opposite faces in turn keep it true.
Every face is worked to its line. (Shown faster than life.)
A round stone: balanced, forgiving, a good first cut.
immersive_jewelry.ponder.shared.brillian: The brilliant: ten faces, the strongest effect and the most waste.
Work each face in its order. Near the depth line, slow down: a face cut too deep stays too deep.
Lift and index deliberately. Symmetry matters more than speed.
The last faces need the most care. (Shown faster than life.)
A brilliant: the most light, the most risk.
immersive_jewelry.ponder.shared.emerald_: The emerald cut: long steps first, then the corners.
Keep the long flats straight. A rocking stone rounds its edges.
Lift before the corners: they are short and chip easily.
Steps and corners finished. (Shown faster than life.)
An emerald cut keeps more stone; its effects last longer.
immersive_jewelry.ponder.shared.cabochon: The cabochon: a smooth dome. Lapis takes it well; a diamond cannot be cut so.
Keep the stone moving: held still, it grinds a flat spot instead of a dome.
Lift and turn to work each region of the dome.
The dome is even all round. (Shown faster than life.)
A cabochon: forgiving, kind to opaque stones, gentle in effect.
immersive_jewelry.ponder.shared.cut_mist: Pressed hard and jerked across the lap: scratches and a rocking stone.
The stone runs hot. Too hot, and it chips.
Dip it in the cooling cup, or simply lift it.
Finished like this, the cut keeps its scratches and chips: a lower quality.
A chipped stone can be recut: mount it and plan again. The size it loses is gone for good.
Smaller, but whole again. The appraisal itself never changes.
immersive_jewelry.ponder.shared.portable: Half done, the stone is lifted and taken off.
Its work travels with it, in the stone itself.
Mounted again, here or at any wheel: the same depths, the same mistakes, the same plan.
Finished where it was left off.
immersive_jewelry.ponder.shared.blank_ro: A ring blank: the frame of a ring.
With Immersive Smithing, blanks are forged in any metal and keep your smithing quality.
Crafting fallbacks exist only when the server enables them. The handbook shows which routes are open.
Pieces with stones, finished or unfinished, are never melted down by recycling.
immersive_jewelry.ponder.shared.folio_an: The folio lists the designs for the frame in the clamp.
The Trilogy Ring is locked: its sketch has not been learned.
Using a Design Sketch teaches its design. Watching this, or reading about it, does not.
The folio brings exactly the matching stones from your inventory to the tray.
immersive_jewelry.ponder.shared.seat_and: Tweezers take one stone from the tray.
Let go over the cup: where and how straight it lands is its seat.
Grip one prong with the pliers and squeeze until it meets the stone, then let go to check.
Opposite prongs in turn, and the stone sits level and secure.
Short of the stone, a prong is loose. Pushed past it, it bends, and may chip a brittle stone.
immersive_jewelry.ponder.shared.bezel_se: A bezel is one continuous rim. The bench's pusher presses it in.
Sweep evenly all the way round: a rim pushed on one side holds the stone crooked.
Held when every section meets the stone.
immersive_jewelry.ponder.shared.three_st: Three diamonds: the same gem, each with its own size, quality and history.
Each socket is closed on its own stone.
No stone copies another: each keeps its own data in the piece.
immersive_jewelry.ponder.shared.atlas_so: Solitaire Ring: one stone, four prongs. Round, brilliant or emerald cut.
immersive_jewelry.ponder.shared.atlas_be: Bezel Ring: one stone in a closed rim. Cabochon, round or emerald cut.
immersive_jewelry.ponder.shared.atlas_tr: Trilogy Ring: three stones of one gem, four prongs each. Learned from a sketch.
immersive_jewelry.ponder.shared.atlas_pe: Pendant Amulet: one stone, six prongs, any cut the gem allows.
immersive_jewelry.ponder.shared.atlas_lo: Locket Amulet: one stone in a bezel. Cabochon or emerald cut.
immersive_jewelry.ponder.shared.atlas_ha: Halo Amulet: three stones of one gem, four prongs each. Learned from a sketch.
immersive_jewelry.ponder.shared.atlas_cu: Cuff Bracelet: one stone in a bezel, any cut the gem allows.
immersive_jewelry.ponder.shared.atlas_li: Link Bracelet: three stones of one gem, four prongs each. Learned from a sketch.
immersive_jewelry.ponder.shared.atlas_si: Simple Circlet: one stone, six prongs, any cut the gem allows.
immersive_jewelry.ponder.shared.atlas_di: Diadem: three stones of one gem, four prongs each. Learned from a sketch.
immersive_jewelry.ponder.shared.polished: Polishing Compound in a jar: one is used, at the first stroke that works the piece.
The cloth goes round in overlapping arcs; the sheen follows what it has covered.
Pausing or packing the work neither charges the compound again nor gives it back.
Polished all over: brighter stones, a frame that wears a little sooner.
immersive_jewelry.ponder.shared.burnishe: The burnisher needs no material at all.
Smooth, controlled passes along the frame.
Every part of the frame must be passed over; one spot rubbed forever never finishes.
Burnished: a satin sheen, a tougher frame, steadier effects.
immersive_jewelry.ponder.shared.antique_: One gunpowder in a jar: the patina.
The brush dabs the patina into the whole piece.
Then the cloth wipes the high points bright; the recesses stay dark.
Antique: darker recesses, far better enchanting.
immersive_jewelry.ponder.shared.quality_: Workmanship combines the metalwork, the cut and the setting. The tooltip shows each.
A defect, such as a loose prong, stays on the piece until it is retightened.
Good work is likely to be good; nothing guarantees a Masterwork.
immersive_jewelry.ponder.shared.retighte: A worn frame and a loose prong: two different problems.
Retightening fixed the prong. The frame is still worn.
Repair, with a nugget of the frame's metal, trues the frame up to its cap.
Every rework lowers the repair cap a little. The history stays on the piece.
immersive_jewelry.ponder.shared.remove_a: Each prong is opened gently with the pliers.
Every stone comes back to the tray as it was: the same stone, not a new roll.
The frame returns to a blank and loses some integrity.
The stones can be set again, in this frame or another.
immersive_jewelry.ponder.shared.refinish: A new finish on a finished piece: burnished over polished.
Refinished. The frame, the setting and the stones are unchanged.
Half-set work packed: an Unfinished piece holds the frame, the stones and the work.
Unpacked at a bench: every closure exactly as it was left.
immersive_jewelry.ponder.shared.wearing_: Rings, amulets, bracelets and circlets are worn in jewelry slots: Curios' or the built-in ones.
By default two rings and one of each other form are active.
One gem, four expressions: a ruby ring builds heat, an amulet saves you, a bracelet rewards a charge.
A broken piece does nothing until it is repaired. It is never destroyed.
immersive_jewelry.ponder.shared.staging_: The staging drawer sits in front of the vise. It keeps four loose stacks you put there yourself.
Open, stacks stay exactly where your hand leaves them. Nothing in the drawer is ever used by itself.
The jars hold supplies. Their counts face you; the mouse wheel puts one in or takes one back.
Prepare stones in the folio moves exactly the stones a design still needs into the tray.
Shut, the drawer hides its stacks and takes nothing. Its list (the drawer key) still reaches every one.
Materials are paid only when they are worked: compound at the first finishing stroke, stones at the first closure.
